postureMeaning: Stands as recommended unless overruled. In on a new-things row commissions it; Out drops it for good.
criterion: Rows are what the biome sheets ADMIT — a lawfulness test, not a worth test. Plant facts are measured from the game's own data; every spawn rate and every purge-by-name call was mine, and your overrules are the point.
invented: Size bins are mine, same as the fauna sheet: small < 1.0 squares on screen · medium 1.0–2.2 (a person is 1.5) · large 2.2–5.0 · TITAN over 5.0 — measured at full growth. Pick a different bin and the plant gets rescaled to match.

True-scale rule: every panel in a biome group shares one px-per-game-square, chosen so the group's biggest plant fits about 460px. Scale is honest WITHIN a group; different groups use different zoom levels. The colonist figure is the same one as the fauna sheet, per your ruling.
'Earth-nameable' was applied by NAME — one agent's reading of each label. A plant whose label reads as a species you could point at on Earth was purged planet-wide; nothing verified that per row.
Several biomes are held together by stand-in donor plants while the plant the sheet really wants sits on the new-art list — those rows say so, and they are placeholders, not designs.
Every spawn rate on every row is agent-chosen.
The new-things list is what the biome sheets DEMAND, not what anyone agreed to build — In on one of those rows commissions it as a real queue item.
The retirement flag works as on the fauna sheet: the ⚑ badge only for mods actually named for retirement; softer wind-down states ride the mod line.
